lessons.title: What is an agent?
lessons.text: A chatbot answers. An agent acts. It is an AI model plus tools plus a loop: think, use a tool, look at the result, repeat until the job is done.

lessons.title: Pick one tiny job
lessons.text: Do not build 'an assistant for everything'. Pick one boring, repeatable task, like sorting your inbox or summarizing a daily report. Small jobs actually work.

lessons.title: Give it tools
lessons.text: Tools are what let an agent touch the world: search, read files, send an email, call an API. Give it only the tools the job needs. Fewer tools means fewer mistakes.

lessons.title: Write clear instructions
lessons.text: Tell the agent its goal, its rules, and what 'done' looks like. Add a few examples. Good instructions beat a fancy model.

lessons.title: Keep a human in the loop
lessons.text: Let the agent draft and you approve, at least at first. Never let it spend money or send things unchecked until you have watched it succeed many times.

lessons.title: You direct, AI types
lessons.text: In 2026 many people build by describing what they want and letting AI write the code. Your job becomes steering: clear goals, small steps, and checking the results.

lessons.title: Specs beat vibes
lessons.text: Vague prompts give vague apps. Write down what it should do, what it looks like, and what counts as done. A short written plan saves hours.

lessons.title: Small steps, then save
lessons.text: Ask for one feature at a time. When something works, commit it with git. Commits are your undo button when a change breaks things.

lessons.title: Learn to read code
lessons.text: You do not need to write everything, but learn to read it. HTML, CSS and a little JavaScript cover most web projects. Reading lets you spot what is wrong.

lessons.title: Ship it and share it
lessons.text: Put it online with a free host like GitHub Pages or Netlify. A live link beats a folder on your laptop, and it is great content to show off.

lessons.title: Chat assistants
lessons.text: Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini are the everyday helpers for writing, thinking, research and learning. Try a few and keep the one that fits how you work.

lessons.title: AI code tools
lessons.text: Tools like Claude Code and Cursor write and edit code inside your project. They are how solo makers build real apps fast.

lessons.title: Search and research
lessons.text: Perplexity and NotebookLM help you find answers and turn your own notes and documents into summaries you can question.

lessons.title: Make images and video
lessons.text: Image and video generators let you create visuals, thumbnails and clips without a studio. Great for content, but always check the usage rules.

lessons.title: Automate the boring stuff
lessons.text: Zapier and n8n connect your apps so repeat tasks run themselves, and AI can sit in the middle to read, sort and write. Start with one workflow.
